criteria.semantics: A native <form> named by its heading (aria-labelledby), its description a hint under it, its fields, choices and buttons inside; a refusal replaces it in place with each field's error beside it.

keyboard.outcome: Moves through the form's controls in order.

criteria.name: The form's label, its heading's text.
criteria.group: The form's label names the group its fields are in.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the heading, labels and fields grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the fields stack in one column under the heading, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <form> element.
The form is named by its heading: aria-labelledby points at it, and it says the form's label.
I SEE the form's heading above its controls: the face emits it as a real <h3>.
WHEN I Tab into the form with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name with its first control.
WHEN I submit the form and it is refused I HEAR the status say so, naming the field, and each error with its field.
WHEN I list the page's landmarks I HEAR the form by its name.

criteria.semantics: The form's label and description above its controls, inside a line border; a refusal says itself in words under them, each field's error beside its field. GPUI exposes no accessibility tree, so no form role reaches assistive technology.

keyboard.outcome: Moves through the form's controls in order.

criteria.name: The form's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my system text size to 200% I SEE the label, the fields and the feedback grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I magnify the window with the system zoom I SEE the form and its border whole.

check.statement: A form adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order; its controls are its stops.
WHEN the form is refused I SEE the refusal in words under it and each error beside its field.
WHEN I Tab into the form with a screen reader (VoiceOver, Orca, Narrator) I HEAR its name and, after a refusal, each error.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit): every HEAR check fails on this face today. Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs), which no CI job runs yet (gpui/README.md, Verification); the rest are reported as not verified.
